messages.content: You are a precise information extraction system. You only output valid JSON.

Extract all entity mentions from the document.

Entity types:
- Person: a named or described human individual or group of people
- Organization: a company, army, government body, team, party or other organised group
- Location: a geographic place: country, city, region, body of water, battlefield, etc.
- Building: a man-made structure or facility: hotel, fort, bridge, airport, etc.
- Product: a man-made object or product: vehicle, ship, aircraft, weapon model, etc.
- Art: a creative work: book, film, song, painting, etc.
- Other: any other named thing relevant to events (e.g. nationalities, named events, ideologies)

Entity annotation rules:
- Annotate named entities AND other mentions that refer to them: nominal phrases ("the plane", "the storm"), subject/object pronouns ("he", "she", "they", "him"), and nationality/group words ("British", "Ottomans").
- Do NOT annotate possessive pronouns ("his", "her", "their", "its"), dates or years ("3 January 1992", "2013").
- Numbers, quantities, ordinals and durations ("13", "two", "3rd", "two days") are entities of type Other.
- Annotate every occurrence, including repeated mentions of the same entity.
- Nationality or group words are typed by what they refer to: a country/place -> Location, an army/state/organisation -> Organization, a people -> Person.

Return JSON: {"entities": [{"text": "<mention copied from the document>", "type": "<entity type>"}]}

### Example 1
Document:
Varig Flight 797 was a flight from Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire to Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. On 3 January 1987 the Boeing 707-320C used for the route crashed while landing killing all 12 crew members and 38 of 39 passengers. When departing Abidjan the aircraft developed problems with its left (No. 1) engine. While returning the aircraft crashed into the jungle 18 km from the airport. The crash site was a rubber plantation. Four days after the disaster, Ahmad Wansa, a British citizen who was injured in the crash, died on board a Swiss aircraft while arriving in Paris; he was going to be transferred to a burn unit in a Paris suburb. The sole remaining survivor, identified as Ivory Coast University Prof. Neuba Yessoh, had burns on less than 20 percent of his body. Yessoh died of heart attack on 4 March 2015 at the age of 72. Varig Flight 254 was a Boeing 737-241, c/n 21006/398, registration on a scheduled passenger flight from São Paulo, Brazil, to Belém, capital city of the state of Pará in the country's North Region, on 3 September 1989. The flight had several intermediate stopovers, the last being in Marabá, Pará. Prior to takeoff from Marabá, the crew entered an incorrect heading into the flight computer, flying deep into a remote area of the Amazon jungle. Attempts to reach an alternative airport were unsuccessful, and the plane eventually ran out of fuel, making a belly landing in the jungle northwest of Rio de Janeiro. Of the 54 passengers and crew, 13 passengers died and many more sustained serious injuries. The survivors were rescued two days later.
